misconceptions.believed: A background-filled badge is a clean degradation of a bracketed one: same width, better appearance where colour is supported.
misconceptions.revealed_by: The depth-invariance check across all four colour depths. Every element matched except the badge row: '[PASS]  [FAIL]' versus ' PASS    FAIL '.
misconceptions.corrected_to: Brackets at every depth, with colour applied to the brackets too, so escape-stripped output is genuinely identical.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: The failure was cheap; the temptation was the lesson. Exit criterion 6 said 'same layout', and the filled badge did preserve layout - one word of amendment would have declared it clean. Noticing the urge to edit the criterion instead of the code is the skill N7 is trying to build.

decisions.decision: Detect stream capabilities rather than assume a terminal
decisions.rationale: Escape codes in a log file are a bug; detection also yields Unicode and animation gating for free.

decisions.decision: Colour applied last, layout computed first
decisions.rationale: Makes depth invariance achievable at all, and lets tests compare readable text.
decisions.seam: The shape of every element method

decisions.decision: Width is a parameter, never read at draw time
decisions.rationale: Testable at any width; nothing silently depends on the 80-column fallback.

decisions.decision: Badges are bracketed at every colour depth
alternatives: Background-filled pill when colour is available
decisions.rationale: Preserves the invariant that colour never changes visible text.

decisions.decision: Build the boss health bar now, before T3 needs it
alternatives: Wait until the boss engine exists
decisions.rationale: The boss fight then renders through the same layer instead of growing a parallel one.

alternatives: curses, which is stdlib and would satisfy N1
decisions.rationale: curses takes over the screen and cannot degrade to a pipe. The game prints; it does not own the terminal.

friction.description: io.StringIO cannot test capability detection: encoding is read-only and isatty() always returns False. Two tests failed on the harness rather than the code.
mock.patch.dict rejects None values, breaking the first attempt at unsetting environment variables.
Whether the layer actually looks good cannot be verified without a human at a real terminal emulator.

handoff.state: T6 LANDED, all eight exit criteria verified. vibecoder/ui.py is the only emitter of escape codes; cli.py contains none. 194 tests green, verify clean on 18 reference runs. New commands: showcase, levels --map. The engine is unchanged and T1 remains LANDED.
handoff.next_action: Unchanged from S001: T2 W1, the container-backed runner behind run_code. T6 was a detour, taken because the friction it resolved was cheap now and expensive once a web front-end exists.

open_questions.question: Should the renderer be injected rather than a module-level UI singleton in cli.py? A web front-end or an output-capturing test has to monkey-patch it today.
Animation is fixed at roughly 0.35s per axis. Does that stay pleasant after ten levels, or become something to sit through? Needs a real player.
The banner is a hand-written ASCII grid. Worth a small figlet-style renderer so world titles can use it too, or is one banner enough?
